2026-10-03 (NEW-STUDIO-ADMISSION-DEFAULT): 0205 APPLIED to production under explicit per-change owner authorization, from the reviewed PR #780 head da15b753f1547da7978ac995a5cc32fbeb0cbf5b, merged as ef611b8460a41613d6b98fcc2932b49f2b831867. hosted_migration_max advances 0204 -> 0205 and the repository returns to PARITY with nothing pending. ONE DEFAULT, TWO COLUMN COMMENTS, AND ZERO ROWS WRITTEN. The migration gives studios.new_client_admission_mode_set_at a `now()` default so a newly created studio is born stamped and is no longer indistinguishable from a pre-0204 legacy row; before this, a brand-new studio's owner was told to choose Waitlist before Open or Closed became available -- a cutover ceremony that belongs only to studios that really did predate 0204. A column default cannot reach a row that already exists, so the migration also carries a bounded apply-time repair for any studio created in the window between the 2026-10-01 census and this apply. AT APPLY TIME THAT WINDOW WAS EMPTY: production held exactly 7 studios, all 7 were census members, the repair had zero candidates, and the server emitted '0205: apply-time repair stamped 0 studio(s)'. The per-candidate guard probe consequently did not execute at all, which is correct by construction -- it exists to prove the guard polices the writes this migration actually makes, and it made none. All 7 studio rows were verified byte-for-byte identical before and after, across mode, set_at, set_by and created_at; the five unstamped legacy studios keep their NULL and their cutover ceremony, and the two owner-stamped studios are untouched. None of the four fail-closed gates tripped (census lineage 7 of 7 present, zero off-shape unstamped non-census rows, no probe needed, post-condition clean). POST-APPLY READS: max(version) 0205, 204 rows, '0205' exactly once, nothing above it; the column default reads now(); both column comments are in pg_description at 1041 and 1193 characters, matching the reviewed source exactly; no table-level comment was added; and there was no object drift -- 6 user triggers unchanged, studios_admission_mode_guard still tgenabled 'O', zero constraints on set_by, 2 indexes. NO APPLICATION CODE WAS DEPLOYED IN SUBSTANCE: lib/booking/new-client-admission.ts is byte-identical to production once comments are stripped, so unlike 0204 this release had no deploy-order constraint. ONE NUMBER WAS DISPLACED AND THE WORK IT NAMED IS STILL OPEN: docs/production/new-client-admission-execution-record.md earmarked '0205' for closing the studios_admission_mode_guard() grant deviation that 0204 left behind. 0205 was used for this change instead and contains zero grant or revoke statements, so that deviation remains open and must be closed by a NEW migration -- 0206 at the earliest, re-censused before anyone authors against it. CARRIED FORWARD, non-blocking: the k_census id set in 0205 is CLOSED and must never grow, because adding an id would protect a studio the census never saw; public.studios still has no INSERT trigger and set_by still has no foreign key, so a direct INSERT can stamp and attribute a row at creation and nothing refuses it -- both column comments now say so, and enforcement would be an INSERT-time check that is deliberately not part of 0205.
